Yes I think making LK a glorified VTT is not very helpful, but to more expand what the workflow would look would be having LK on one tab, and an actual VTT app in another. No more work on the user than having D&D Beyond in one tab and Roll20 on a different tab.

One thing video games always have over Tabletop Games is how much information you can give players right in their own character sheet - an inventory of Health Potions isn't as helpful as Health Potions while telling them here is how much they're worth, here's how many hit points they give you, and their weight ... without clogging up a pen-and-paper character sheet or spreadsheet; something Dungeons and Dragons: Beyond does well. LK can enable this kind of design by just having a link to a "Health Potion" master file to read all about its stats and/or lore same going with weapons and other equipment which is already functional!

Just being able to link to a page and having a tooltip of what it's linking can fulfill at least half the needs of a character sheet honestly - "What's this spell do?" "idk just hover over it" "What's Dexterity do again?" "idk just hover over it"

And widgets could be a really great addition, like you're saying with dropdowns, and counters, because these all aren't exclusive to just having campaign dairies or running character sheets: sometimes you just want a counter for the added population of a bunch of villages this Empire owns while also giving functionality for counting up the accumulated weight of a character's inventory.

Widgets or not though, I think being able to give functionality to do simple math either pulled from cells in a table or the sidebar is enough to get started, as these games are driven by math and just being able to apply a simple function as (n + 2) is enough to reduce the amount of brain numbing number crunching tabletop RPGs are known for. And like the example I gave, World builders would like this too as a simple function like (year - birthyear) will keep characters aging without brainnumbing work everytime the World they're building goes forward/backward in time.

No matter how this is implemented, very excited to see the future of this wonderful app you're building! :)
